title: AstraNova POC scoping - open model shortlist & benchmarks
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Platform: Zoom (recording on)

Summary:
- POC scoping to evaluate open models for clinical note classification + multilingual support (EN, ES, FR).
- Success criteria: >92% macro-F1 on labeled clinical test set, inference latency <180ms p95 on hosted, and cost target <$0.0008/token equivalent.
- Workload: 500k inference calls/month with 80% short (<=128 tokens) and 20% long (<=1024 tokens).
- Shortlist: Mistral-instruct-ish family, Llama-2-13B (quantized), Falcon-40B-instruct (distilled variant), and RedPajama-Chat 13B.
- Next steps: Redwood to run 3-model benchmark with AstraNova sample dataset, share SLO/pricing sketch, and schedule dedicated benchmark run on Nov 10.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, model selection, privacy/VPC needs.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood here, I'm the AE on this. Quick intros?
00:08 Priya Singh: Hi I'm Priya, Head of ML at AstraNova. We're focused on automating triage and coding of clinical notes.
00:13 Diego Marquez: Diego, CTO. We're evaluating open models because of cost and controllable deployment.
00:20 Liam O'Connor: Liam, solutions engineer. I'll dig into latency/cost tradeoffs and benchmarking plan.
00:26 Hannah Lee: Hannah, SRE. Interested in VPC, KMS, and audit/logging.
00:32 Maya Chen: Great. Goal today: scope a POC — what success looks like, workload size, which open models to try, and timelines.

03:00 Priya Singh: For success criteria, primary is classification quality on our labeled test set — we want an F1 at or above 0.92 macro. Secondary, latency p95 under 180ms for short requests, and cost per token equivalent needs to be <0.0008.
03:25 Liam O'Connor: That makes sense. Clarifying: when you say p95 180ms, that's on our prod-like traffic or during bursts?
03:35 Priya Singh: Ideally prod-like steady state. Bursts can be higher.
03:40 Liam O'Connor: Ok. For steady state we can prototype on Redwood Hosted to get baseline then move to Dedicated if cost SLOs need reserved capacity.

07:12 Diego Marquez: Our monthly volume estimate is roughly 500k inferences — average input lengths skew short, 80% under 128 tokens, 20% up to 1k tokens for consolidation tasks.
07:30 Maya Chen: Good, that sizing helps with batching and kernel selection. We'll include both short-path and long-path in benchmarks.

10:05 Priya Singh: On domain specifics, clinical language includes a fair bit of jargon and occasional Spanish/Portuguese. Multilingual performance is important but primary is English clinical accuracy.
10:20 Liam O'Connor: We'll include a multilingual evaluation slice (EN/ES/FR) and a clinical jargon set. For models, open options we commonly benchmark: Llama-2 13B (quantized 4-bit), Mistral 7B/Blend (instruct tuned), Falcon 40B distilled variants, and RedPajama-Chat 13B. Each has different tradeoffs for cost vs quality.

13:45 Diego Marquez: Any concerns about hallucination/structured labels? We need reliable structured outputs for downstream billing systems.
13:55 Liam O'Connor: We'll instrument quality checks and use deterministic decoding for structured fields; also consider model prompting patterns and few-shot examples to reduce hallucination. We'll include an eval metric for structural integrity.

17:00 Priya Singh: For PII and compliance — can Redwood run the POC on Hosted with guaranteed zero-persistence or do we need Private?
17:12 Maya Chen: Hosted has configurable retention and enterprise customers can opt for no-data-retention plus logging controls. For stronger guarantees we can run in Private (VPC) or Dedicated where you control keys (KMS). For benchmarking you can share a de-identified sample with us and we can run hosted baseline.
17:35 Hannah Lee: We will provide de-id data first. If results look promising we'll want a VPC deployment and customer-managed KMS for the pilot. Also need SOC 2 Type II and audit logs — are those available?
17:50 Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood provides SOC 2 Type II documentation, audit logs, and SSO/SAML for entitlements. We'll attach the security pack.

22:10 Liam O'Connor: On benchmarks — propose three-phase: quick host baseline (3 models, small sample), full benchmark (50-100k samples across slices), and performance run (latency/cost under production-like concurrency). The quick baseline can be done in ~3 business days after we get the sample. Full benchmark takes 2 weeks.
22:35 Priya Singh: Sounds good. Timeline wise we want pilot by mid-December. Is that realistic?
22:45 Maya Chen: Yes, if we start sample exchange and sign the POC terms early November, pilot mid-December is achievable.

26:05 Diego Marquez: Model shortlist — which models do you recommend for clinical & multilingual?
26:12 Liam O'Connor: Recommendation hierarchy: 1) Mistral-7B-Instruct or similar for very cost-sensitive short text classification (good latency). 2) Llama-2-13B (quantized 4-bit) for stronger English quality and decent multilingual capability. 3) Falcon-40B distilled variant for highest base-capacity on complex prompts but more expensive; consider only if 13B variants fall short. 4) RedPajama-Chat 13B as a parity/open-weights candidate to test community models. We'll run all three in quick baseline.
26:55 Priya Singh: Any guidance on quantization risks for structured outputs?
27:05 Liam O'Connor: 4-bit quantization (Q4) works for many classification tasks but we will validate against your labeled set — sometimes long-form generation quality can degrade. We'll include an evaluation slice for long prompts.

31:40 Hannah Lee: Infrastructure question: if we move to Dedicated, can we pin GPUs and have predictable throughput? We need autoscaling with burst to avoid downtime.
31:50 Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with autoscaling and burst policies. We'll include SLA latency targets in the POC contract draft.

35:20 Priya Singh: What will the Redwood benchmark deliverable look like?
35:28 Liam O'Connor: Deliverables: benchmark report (accuracy by slice, latency p50/p95/p99, cost estimates normalized to tokens, recommendations for quantization and model), raw logs (redacted), and a runbook for deployment config.
35:45 Diego Marquez: Will you include calibration on prompt engineering and few-shot templates?
35:50 Liam O'Connor: Yes, we'll test 0-shot, few-shot, and instruction-tuned prompts and surface the best templates.

39:10 Maya Chen: Recap and next steps — we're proposing: 1) AstraNova to send de-identified sample dataset (20k labeled rows) + traffic profile by Nov 3; 2) Redwood runs quick baseline (3 models) and shares results by Nov 7; 3) schedule full benchmark and performance run week of Nov 10 (needs signed POC terms); 4) security pack and SOC 2 docs shared by Redwood.

40:00 Priya Singh: We can get the dataset to you by Nov 3. We'll review POC terms with legal this week.
40:10 Diego Marquez: We'll aim to have sign-off for the POC purchase order by Nov 6.
40:20 Hannah Lee: I'll review the security pack and circle back on KMS requirements.

46:30 Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll send the benchmark template and pricing sketch today.
46:40 Priya Singh: Thanks, talk soon.

End of recording.
